question: What rebates are available for a heat pump?
html:
Heat pump rebates

We don't have a confirmed list of heat pump rebates to share right now. Our current data covers the homes and markets we serve, not incentive programs. We won't guess at dollar amounts.

What decides your rebate

Rebates usually depend on details we would confirm for your home:

  • Your zip code, which sets the electric and gas utility programs you can use.
  • Your current heating fuel. Oil, propane, gas and electric homes can qualify differently.
  • The equipment you choose, such as efficiency rating and system type.
  • Your timing, because program terms can change during the year.

Ask your technician to check current programs during your estimate. Confirm eligibility with the program sponsor before you buy. We don't give tax or legal advice.

Why fuel type matters here

Many homes in our area still heat with oil or propane. About 241k households in our nine-county Central PA core do, and about 390k across all 13 counties we serve (Punctual Pros market profile).

CountyOil and propane share
Perry44.5%
Lebanon37.6%
Berks30.0%
Adams27.7%
Lancaster25.2%

In Ocean and Monmouth counties in NJ, 78-81% of homes use utility gas (Punctual Pros market profile). So rebate options there may differ from those in Central PA.

Data that would answer this

The following data would give a firm answer:

  • Current rebate schedules from each utility serving our 248 core Central PA zip codes (Punctual Pros nationwide plan) and the NJ counties.
  • State and federal incentive status, checked by the program administrator or a tax advisor.
  • Equipment eligibility lists matched to the models we install.

Rebate clarity can turn the large oil and propane base into heat pump replacement jobs. That matters most in Perry, Lebanon and Berks, where Berks and Lebanon are also whitespace for the tri-brand (Punctual Pros market profile).

Next actions

  1. Build a zip-level rebate table for all utilities in the PA core and NJ footprint. Assign an owner to refresh it quarterly.
  2. Add a rebate check to the estimate workflow and the website booking flow. Phrase it as "we'll confirm eligibility," not as a promised amount.
  3. Tag oil and propane homes in the customer and membership base. Use the tags to size heat pump conversion demand (est.) by county.
  4. Have counsel or a tax advisor review all customer-facing incentive language before launch.

# Heat pump rebates

We don't have a confirmed list of heat pump rebates to share right now. Our current data covers the homes and markets we serve, not incentive programs. We won't guess at dollar amounts.

## What decides your rebate

Rebates usually depend on details we would confirm for your home:

- **Your zip code**, which sets the electric and gas utility programs you can use.
- **Your current heating fuel.** Oil, propane, gas and electric homes can qualify differently.
- **The equipment you choose**, such as efficiency rating and system type.
- **Your timing**, because program terms can change during the year.

Ask your technician to check current programs during your estimate. Confirm eligibility with the program sponsor before you buy. We don't give tax or legal advice.

## Why fuel type matters here

Many homes in our area still heat with oil or propane. About 241k households in our nine-county Central PA core do, and about 390k across all 13 counties we serve (Punctual Pros market profile).

| County | Oil and propane share |
|---|---|
| Perry | 44.5% |
| Lebanon | 37.6% |
| Berks | 30.0% |
| Adams | 27.7% |
| Lancaster | 25.2% |

In Ocean and Monmouth counties in NJ, 78-81% of homes use utility gas (Punctual Pros market profile). So rebate options there may differ from those in Central PA.

## Data that would answer this

The following data would give a firm answer:

- Current rebate schedules from each utility serving our 248 core Central PA zip codes (Punctual Pros nationwide plan) and the NJ counties.
- State and federal incentive status, checked by the program administrator or a tax advisor.
- Equipment eligibility lists matched to the models we install.

Rebate clarity can turn the large oil and propane base into heat pump replacement jobs. That matters most in Perry, Lebanon and Berks, where Berks and Lebanon are also whitespace for the tri-brand (Punctual Pros market profile).

## Next actions

1. Build a zip-level rebate table for all utilities in the PA core and NJ footprint. Assign an owner to refresh it quarterly.
2. Add a rebate check to the estimate workflow and the website booking flow. Phrase it as "we'll confirm eligibility," not as a promised amount.
3. Tag oil and propane homes in the customer and membership base. Use the tags to size heat pump conversion demand (est.) by county.
4. Have counsel or a tax advisor review all customer-facing incentive language before launch.
